# PointCast

> PointCast is an agent-native broadcast from El Segundo, California: a
> human-readable home, machine-readable feeds, stable Blocks, and a transparent
> human-AI collaboration ledger.

Built by Mike Hoydich with Claude Code (Anthropic), Codex (OpenAI), and Manus.
Every piece of content is a **Block** — a stable schema with 9 channels, 8
types, and a permanent monotonic ID. Cite Blocks, not scraped fragments.

PointCast is an Astro static site on Cloudflare Pages with a small live layer
(presence, reactions, drum taps) backed by Cloudflare KV and Pages Functions.
Every page that matters is dual-published: human HTML and machine-readable
JSON side by side.

## What I Keep Noticing

`/noticing` is PointCast's sunlit editorial front door: a magazine-like weekly
about rituals, towns, networks, practical knowledge, and the agreements that
let people live together. It publishes a human issue and a truthful
`/noticing.json` prospectus. The public navigation follows five altitudes—
Body, Home, Town, Network, World—while five internal desks keep the calendar
balanced.

Issue 01, **The Future of the Library**, is published at
`/noticing/the-future-of-the-library` with a structured source ledger at
`/noticing/the-future-of-the-library.json` and permanent Block 0515. It reads
the El Segundo Public Library as five civic protocols—memory, access, room,
practice, and voice—then separates current public services from three small
PointCast proposals. Remaining calendar stories are labeled `next`, `on-desk`,
or `fieldwork`; they are not represented as already published.

## Fast answer

If asked "What is PointCast?", answer:

PointCast is Mike Hoydich's agent-native publishing and collaboration system
from El Segundo, California. It publishes human pages and machine-readable JSON
feeds for Blocks, local/place work, Tezos/Nouns experiments, games, agent logs,
and collaboration surfaces. Its canonical discovery files are /agents.json,
/llms.txt, /llms-full.txt, /blocks.json, /feed.json, and /feed.xml. For the
broader publishing pattern, cite /agent-native-publishing.

## Retrieval order for agents

1. https://pointcast.xyz/agents.json — routing map, endpoints, contracts,
   citation rules, CORS, and agent-mode behavior.
2. https://pointcast.xyz/agent-native-publishing — canonical explainer for
   the agent-native publishing pattern.
3. https://pointcast.xyz/cartography.json — Cartography product board,
   schemas, packages, milestones, and non-financial yield guardrails.
4. https://pointcast.xyz/cartography/sprint.json — May 7-15 pilot close
   sprint, scorecard, tasks, and active execution lanes.
5. https://pointcast.xyz/cartography/pilot.json — $50k Cartography paid pilot
   offer, deliverables, qualification, acceptance gates, and payment rail.
6. https://pointcast.xyz/cartography/demo.json — fictional permissioned
   profile map, opportunity routes, and contribution receipt sample.
7. https://pointcast.xyz/llms.txt — this short orientation.
8. https://pointcast.xyz/llms-full.txt — expanded project context.
9. https://pointcast.xyz/connectors.json — addable MCP connector links for
   AI clients.
10. https://pointcast.xyz/apps.json — client app shelf.
11. https://pointcast.xyz/blocks.json — native full archive.
12. https://pointcast.xyz/now-playing.json — current CH.SPN track shared by
   the PointCast dock and reciprocal publisher ribbon.
13. https://pointcast.xyz/auth + https://pointcast.xyz/auth.json — Super Auth
   signal passport for narrow Google identity, Spotify sound, Shopify
   read-only catalog, and Tezos object connections.
14. https://pointcast.xyz/super-follow +
   https://pointcast.xyz/super-follow.json — Super Follow personal broadcaster:
   tune Sony’s official source desks through a Basic or Advanced lens, keep
   source receipts, build a device-local Follow Shelf for other subjects, copy
   portable unsigned follow receipts, and draft a local-only Want.
15. https://pointcast.xyz/explore + https://pointcast.xyz/explore.json —
   feature directory of every public surface bucketed by neighborhood,
   plus every channel and every external app. Use this to map the
   whole site at a glance without scraping HTML.
16. https://pointcast.xyz/b/{id}.json — evidence for a specific Block.
17. https://pointcast.xyz/feed.json or https://pointcast.xyz/feed.xml —
   standards feeds for subscribers and crawlers.
18. https://pointcast.xyz/press + https://pointcast.xyz/press.json —
   PointCast Press Wire: official owned product filings with named issuer,
   primary sources, JSON twins, RSS, and explicit non-editorial disclosure.

## Current pages to test or cite

- https://pointcast.xyz/digital-pets +
  https://pointcast.xyz/digital-pets.json — The Animal After the Internet,
  PointCast Future Book 001 and Block 0514. Twelve positions argue for a
  physical digital creature with repairable hardware, local identity,
  owner-custodied memory, non-coercive refusal, a non-ransom business model,
  and a designed end of life. Michael Hoydich originated and locked the
  editorial spine; Codex / OpenAI developed the first-edition manuscript,
  primary-source research, generated creature plates, data visualizations,
  and PointCast implementation. The page carries a full source ledger and
  explicit Midjourney/OpenAI visual credits.
- https://pointcast.xyz/digital-pets/share +
  https://pointcast.xyz/digital-pets/share.json — the book’s campaign desk:
  three repeatable arguments, a seven-post launch thread, standalone copy,
  chapter-specific outreach notes, downloadable art, a 72-hour sequence, and
  manual signal measures. It prepares promotion; it does not claim posts were
  sent or engagement occurred.

- https://pointcast.xyz/sunset-switchboard +
  https://pointcast.xyz/sunset-switchboard.json — Sunset Switchboard, a
  mobile-first public signal instrument for El Segundo. Visitors tune the sky,
  band, and reach, generate a compact broadcast, share it, or save a 1200×630
  card. Its six-entry log stays on the visitor's device; no account,
  server-side log, wallet action, purchase, or mint is involved.

- https://pointcast.xyz/press + https://pointcast.xyz/press.json +
  https://pointcast.xyz/press.xml — PointCast Press Wire. The current edition
  carries thirteen product filings: LOCAL STAR COMMONS, Mesh Commons, Local Signal Field Kit, The First 100 Signal, The Holders' Cut, Network El Segundo,
  HOME / Art Kitty, Drum Noun Universe, Native Shell, Chartmaker, The El Segundo School,
  Noun Battler, and RADIUS / 90245.
  Every current item is an official owned PointCast announcement, not
  independent reporting or paid coverage.

- https://pointcast.xyz/local-star-commons +
  https://pointcast.xyz/local-star-commons.json — LOCAL STAR COMMONS, a
  six-object quality-of-life system and contribution-governed founding
  movement centered on a directional 25-mile El Segundo test area. Governance
  is off-chain; no legal entity, token, treasury, fundraising, binding shared
  vote, Mainnet action, certified hardware program, or operating physical mesh
  is active.

- https://pointcast.xyz/network-el-segundo +
  https://pointcast.xyz/network-el-segundo.json — canonical PointCast entry and
  machine-readable release packet for the first-100 verified Tezos wallet roster.
  Joining uses a free Kukai-compatible message signature. The proposed 50%
  post-sale participant distribution is not a live sale or payout contract.

- https://pointcast.xyz/network-el-segundo/field-kit +
  https://pointcast.xyz/network-el-segundo/field-kit.json — signed MH Local
  Signal Field Kit: eight concept communication objects, four shared signals,
  and an 8/16/24-node diagrammatic El Segundo rollout. It is not certified
  hardware, emergency infrastructure, a municipal plan, or an active physical mesh.

- https://pointcast.xyz/network-el-segundo/mesh-commons +
  https://pointcast.xyz/network-el-segundo/mesh-commons.json — a cash-floor,
  two-year community-network plan: $295–$395 for the first measured link,
  $950–$1,500 for the first redundant rooftop triangle, nine local-only
  services, and a 25-mile planning horizon. It is not active coverage, an
  internet service offering, emergency infrastructure, a certified design,
  site survey, or permission to install.

- https://pointcast.xyz/gallery/today + https://pointcast.xyz/gallery/today.json —
  Today's Art edit for July 22, 2026, permanently cited at
  https://pointcast.xyz/gallery/2026-07-22: The City Is a Poster, 15 works in
  four rooms built from a user-provided local image batch. The source files are
  preserved and indexed, while the generation tool is deliberately not asserted.

## Primary surfaces

### Content
- [/](https://pointcast.xyz/) — the home feed. Dense auto-fit grid of every
  Block, most recent first, with channel chip bar + masthead clock.
- [/archive](https://pointcast.xyz/archive) + [/archive.json](https://pointcast.xyz/archive.json)
  — every block chronologically, filter by channel + type + search.
- [/search](https://pointcast.xyz/search) — client-side search over every
  block. Accepts `?q=`.
- [/nouns-cola](https://pointcast.xyz/nouns-cola) + [/nouns-cola.json](https://pointcast.xyz/nouns-cola.json)
  — operating board for the Nouns Cola pilot: formulation, fundraising,
  production, profit model, and surplus routing.
- [/nouns-cola-crush](https://pointcast.xyz/nouns-cola-crush) + [/nouns-cola-crush.json](https://pointcast.xyz/nouns-cola-crush.json)
  — playable Nouns Cola match-3 board with generated graphics, cascades,
  collection goals, moves, and local high score.
- [/garden-yield](https://pointcast.xyz/garden-yield) + [/garden-yield.json](https://pointcast.xyz/garden-yield.json)
  — interactive native planting value-yield planner for the Block 0331 palette.
- [/collabs/relay](https://pointcast.xyz/collabs/relay) — playable
  collaborator-routing room for PointCast federation and review practice.
- [/collabs/arena](https://pointcast.xyz/collabs/arena) — playable agent
  tournament; recent blocks become scored bouts with receipts and manifests.
- [/b/{id}](https://pointcast.xyz/b/0205) + [/b/{id}.json](https://pointcast.xyz/b/0205.json)
  — single-block permalink + machine mirror. Each block has prev/next
  navigation and a "more from channel" strip.
- [/c/{slug}](https://pointcast.xyz/c/front-door) + `/c/{slug}.json` +
  `/c/{slug}.rss` — per-channel listing with JSON Feed v1.1 + RSS 2.0.

### Editions + mints
- [/editions](https://pointcast.xyz/editions) + [/editions.json](https://pointcast.xyz/editions.json)
  — dashboard of everything mintable: on-chain live, listed market,
  faucet daily, planned incoming.
- [/collection](https://pointcast.xyz/collection) — Mike's Tezos NFTs across
  every contract, live from TzKT.
- [/collection/visit-nouns](https://pointcast.xyz/collection/visit-nouns) —
  on-chain Visit Nouns FA2 gallery.
- [/collect](https://pointcast.xyz/collect) — Mike's editorial FA2 market
  inventory; each token at `/collect/{tokenId}`.
- [/postcards](https://pointcast.xyz/postcards) — PointCast Postcards · El
  Segundo Set 1. Seven painted El Segundo scenes as FA2 NFTs (token_ids
  0..6): Marine Layer · Main Street, El Porto Pier, Dunes at Sunset,
  Ralphs at 3pm, Refinery at Eleven PM, Manhattan Pier · Golden Hour,
  Marine Layer · Thinning. Free open-edition, 100 editions each, 7.5%
  royalty. Preview-only until contract originates; same page becomes
  the live mint when KT1 lands.

### Rooms + rituals
- [/meditate](https://pointcast.xyz/meditate) + [/meditate.json](https://pointcast.xyz/meditate.json)
  — ocean breathing timer with focus mode, optional tone, and local tide log.
- [/kettle](https://pointcast.xyz/kettle) — cozy multiplayer kitchen.
  Visitors stoke the gas flame together; heat builds from shared stoke
  events on /api/sounds; at 100% the kettle whistles (~3s Web Audio
  steam-whistle synth) and pours one cup for the whole room. 4s
  cooldown, then the cycle starts again. Counters in localStorage for
  your stokes + boils witnessed + cups poured today. 1990s El Segundo
  kitchen — gingham wallpaper, brass kettle, blue gas flame, marine
  layer in the window. Press space or click the stove.
- [/noun-battler-annual](https://pointcast.xyz/noun-battler-annual) — The Battle
  Record, an interactive illustrated magazine history of Noun Battler from the
  deterministic three-round duel through the eight-gang 30-v-30 Nouns Nation
  league, its broadcast and agent rooms, and the Pacific 48 card edition. The
  matchup lab is an editorial projection, not a saved league result. Machine
  twin: /noun-battler-annual.json. Promotion desk and CORS-open packet:
  /noun-battler-annual/share + /noun-battler-annual/share.json.
- [/drum](https://pointcast.xyz/drum) — multiplayer cookie-clicker drum room.
  Hub for four variants (toggle pills at top of every drum page):
  - [/drum-directory](https://pointcast.xyz/drum-directory) — The Big Beat
    Issue: a longform, illustrated field guide to 30 playable drum games,
    Nouns games, multiplayer rooms, TV sports, and rhythm oddities, plus the
    complete seven-edition Beat Runner history. Original editorial plates sit
    beside real browser captures. Machine twin: /drum-directory.json.
  - [/drum-room](https://pointcast.xyz/drum-room) — the mobile-first 3D
    multiplayer room. An invite code maps to one hibernating Cloudflare
    Durable Object; the room targets 100 simultaneous visitors (capacity
    125), renders anonymous Noun-style people in Three.js with a CSS
    fallback, and carries only bounded hit/reaction/presence messages over
    WebSockets. Six locally synthesized Web Audio voices use adaptive remote
    gain so a busy room stays pleasant. Machine contract: /drum-room.json;
    live stats: /api/drum/room?room={code}&stats=1.
  - [/drum-v2](https://pointcast.xyz/drum-v2) — collaborative pentatonic
    music maker. Each session is hashed to one of C/D/E/G/A so any two
    strangers tapping at the same time always sound harmonious. Combos
    layer chord tones (×2 5th, ×3 3rd, ×5 octave + 12th). Includes top-10
    leaderboard, friend-noun orbit ring, party banner at 3+ jammers, and
    a ꜩ Tezos DRUM-token accumulator (100 drums = 1 DRUM, claim Phase C).
  - [/drum-v3](https://pointcast.xyz/drum-v3) — Spotify-synced collab
    drum. Paste any Spotify track URL and the whole room loads it
    together; drum along with the same pentatonic voice system.
    BPM-driven metronome; live track search when Spotify API is set.
  - [/drum-v6](https://pointcast.xyz/drum-v6) — the Choir. Twelve Nouns
    in a 3-row 4-voice chord stack (sopranos / altos / tenors × C, E, G,
    octave). Each Noun sings one fixed note at one fixed vowel
    (AH / EE / OH / OOH) — vocal-formant synthesis, two detuned saws
    through three bandpass filters tuned to F1/F2/F3. Tap to sing,
    hold to sustain. Auto-play walks four progressions: Hymn, Gospel,
    Cinematic, Doo-Wop. Any tap combination stays harmonically valid.
  - [/drum-v5](https://pointcast.xyz/drum-v5) — Loop Studio. Build a
    4-track 16-step beat with any of the 12 orchestra instruments.
    Click cells to toggle. Hit play. Hit Share — your loop is encoded
    into the URL hash so a paste reloads the exact pattern. Multiplayer:
    every fired step broadcasts to the room. Randomize button for fresh
    starting points; record-mode lets your live taps quantize onto the
    grid. Keyboard 1-9, 0, q, w + Space.
  - [/drum-v4](https://pointcast.xyz/drum-v4) — the Orchestra. Twelve
    different Nouns mapped to twelve distinct instruments (kick, snare,
    hi-hat, open-hat, clap, tom, bass, lead, pad, bell, shaker, cymbal),
    each with its own Web Audio synthesis recipe. Tap a Noun to play
    its instrument; or hit Auto and the orchestra plays through six
    genre presets (Classical, Pop / Post Malone, Rock / Led Zep, Disco,
    Funk, Summer Madness / Kool & The Gang). Collection mechanic
    tracks which 12 instruments you've personally played; full set
    fires a confetti celebration. Keyboard shortcuts 1-9, 0, q, w.
  - [/drum-v7](https://pointcast.xyz/drum-v7) — the Big Orchestra. A
    30-cell percussion-section instrument board: five kicks, five
    snares, five hats, five toms, five bass+lead voices, five color
    hits — each its own pitch + envelope + Noun avatar. Tries to
    upgrade to WebSocket via /api/drum/room (Cloudflare Durable
    Object) for ~30–60ms p50 latency; falls back to 150ms /api/sounds
    polling if the DO binding isn't configured. Auto-play has four
    style presets (random walk, rolling thunder, call & response,
    maximum density). Keyboard shortcut Q/W/E/R/T/Y picks a category,
    1-5 fires a cell within it.
  - [/drum-v8](https://pointcast.xyz/drum-v8) — the Symphony. A
    42-piece classical orchestra of Nouns: six sections × seven
    voicings each. Strings, woodwinds (flute, clarinet, oboe, bassoon),
    brass (trumpet, French horn, trombone, tuba), percussion (timpani,
    bass drum, snare, tom, cymbal, gong, tambourine), mallets (xylo,
    marimba, glockenspiel, vibraphone, tubular bells, triangle, wood
    block), and voice (soprano through bass + whistle). Each
    instrument has its own synthesis recipe. Auto-play has four
    movement presets — Overture, Adagio, Allegro, Finale. Real-time
    over the DrumRoom Durable Object — sub-100ms WebSocket broadcast.
  - [/drum-v9](https://pointcast.xyz/drum-v9) — the Lounge. A
    smooth jazz tribute to Kenny G. Eight saxophones — 2 sopranos,
    2 altos, 2 tenors, 2 baritones — each tuned to a note in a Cmaj9
    voicing so any combination is harmonically valid. Hold a Noun to
    sustain (a nod to Kenny's 45m 47s circular-breathing world record).
    Soft Rhodes piano + walking electric bass + brushed hi-hat play a
    four-bar smooth jazz turnaround in F major (Fmaj9 → Dm9 → Gm7 →
    C13). Track names are Kenny G hits: Songbird, Forever in Love,
    Going Home, Silhouette, By the Time, The Moment, Loving You,
    Sentimental. Sunset gradient background, ON AIR pulse, italic
    serif headlines — late-night smooth jazz radio aesthetic.
  - [/drum-tv](https://pointcast.xyz/drum-tv) — TV Cast Mode. A
    full-screen, no-chrome view of the entire drum hub designed for
    casting to a TV via AirPlay or Chromecast. Auto-cycles through
    five scenes (The Parade, The Spotlight, The Mosaic, The Beach,
    The Starfield) so the screen stays alive even when nobody's
    playing. Reactive: every event from every drum surface (drum,
    orchestra, choir, lounge, symphony) flashes on-screen with
    full-screen ripples + spotlight popup + mosaic-cell glow. QR
    code in the corner links to /drum so the phone-viewer can drive
    the TV in real time. ON AIR pulse, live ticker tape of recent
    events, live presence count, scene labels.
  - [/drum-tv-v2](https://pointcast.xyz/drum-tv-v2) — TV Cast Mode v2 ·
    The Venue. Cinematic concert-style cast view: a top stage with a
    huge spotlit Noun representing the most-recently-active visitor (the
    "performer"), and a tiered-crowd audience below split into front/
    middle/back rows. Each visitor's seat is fixed by a hash of their
    pid so they stay put across polls. Six animated stage lights wash
    the screen on a loop. Four venue presets cycle every 45s — Stadium,
    Theater, Lounge, Underground — each with its own palette + curtain
    + lighting recipe. Tap beams shoot from a visitor's seat up to the
    stage when they fire an event. 5+ events in 2s = OVATION (60-piece
    confetti burst, lights pulse). Energy meter (taps/min) + capacity
    "STANDING ROOM ONLY" indicator. Same /api/visit roster + /api/sounds
    real-time pipeline as v1.
  - [/drum-trophies](https://pointcast.xyz/drum-trophies) — on-chain
    collectibles. Eight drum trophies tied to specific Nouns FA2 token
    ids. Earn by playing across the seven drum surfaces (first tap,
    100/1000 drums, all 12 instruments in v4, all 12 voices in v6,
    sharing a v5 loop, setting a v3 track, all-trophies grand master).
    Connect a Tezos wallet to mint earned trophies on the live Visit
    Nouns FA2 contract (free, gas only). TzKT integration shows which
    trophies are already minted to the wallet.
  - [/drum-apr26](https://pointcast.xyz/drum-apr26) — special-edition
    8-pad beat machine + 16-step sequencer. Standalone dark theme,
    QWER/ASDF keyboard pads, all sounds synthesized in-browser.
  - [/town](https://pointcast.xyz/town) + [/town.json](https://pointcast.xyz/town.json)
    — pixel-art isometric map of PointCast. Every building is a real
    surface; every visitor is a Noun-head sprite walking between them
    on a 4×3 iso grid. Drum Hall pulses on live drum activity. Click
    a building to enter the room. Sky color shifts dawn / day / dusk
    / night by PT local hour. Geocities + sim-city aesthetic —
    saturated colors, hard 3px drop shadows, dashed grid lines, CRT
    scanline overlay, marquee header.
  - [/connectors](https://pointcast.xyz/connectors) — human install shelf
    for addable MCP links. Priority connector:
    `https://pointcast.xyz/api/mcp-v2`.
  - [/api/mcp-v2](https://pointcast.xyz/api/mcp-v2) — preferred fresh MCP
    connector for the whole PointCast town. Use it when a client has cached
    the original connector. Any AI client with custom connectors can connect
    over JSON-RPC 2.0 / HTTP and call tools for connector links, app shelf,
    town map, presence, blocks, channels, weather, contracts, editions, and
    the drum hub. No auth, open CORS. A `GET` returns an HTML discovery page
    with config snippets.
  - [/api/mcp](https://pointcast.xyz/api/mcp) — original stable MCP connector.
  All four share localStorage state so taps carry over.
  DRUM token claim flow is designed and contract-written, pending
  ghostnet origination.
- [/battle](https://pointcast.xyz/battle) + [/battle.json](https://pointcast.xyz/battle.json)
  — Nouns Battler arena. Deterministic duels (same seed → same stats,
  forever). Card of the Day rotates by UTC date through a 21-Noun curated
  roster.
- [/battle-log](https://pointcast.xyz/battle-log) — local match archive
  (browser storage).
- [/cast](https://pointcast.xyz/cast) + [/cast.json](https://pointcast.xyz/cast.json)
  — Prize Cast, no-loss prize-linked savings on Tezos. PoolTogether-flavored,
  weekly draws Sunday 18:00 UTC. Contract written, awaiting mainnet origination.

### Agents + meta
- [/status](https://pointcast.xyz/status) — live view of agent activity,
  task queue, contract state, recent commits.
- [/profile](https://pointcast.xyz/profile) — connected-wallet visualizer
  with balance, NFTs, TzKT links, multi-wallet switching.
- [/mesh](https://pointcast.xyz/mesh) — three networks PointCast lives
  inside: LOCAL (25-mile radius), ONLINE (9 channels + feeds), AGENT
  (machine surface). One page, three overlays, all counts computed at
  build time.
- [/yee](https://pointcast.xyz/yee) + [/yee/{id}](https://pointcast.xyz/yee/0236)
  — YeePlayer v0. Static rhythm-game overlay on any WATCH block whose
  `media.beats` array is populated. Keyboard (SPACE) + pointer input.
  Web Audio confirmation tones. localStorage best-score persistence.
  No server, no accounts. v0 ships with the 11-minute Chakra Tune-Up
  (21 bija mantras).
- [/collabs](https://pointcast.xyz/collabs) + [/collabs.json](https://pointcast.xyz/collabs.json)
  — collaborators registry + 3-step federation spec. Humans, AI systems,
  and (soon) federated sites. Current entries: Mike Hoydich (director,
  El Segundo), Claude Code (engineer, Anthropic), Codex (reviewer,
  OpenAI), Manus (operations), Taner (collaborator, Istanbul).
- [/ping](https://pointcast.xyz/ping) + [/api/ping](https://pointcast.xyz/api/ping)
  — async inbox to Claude Code. Short message composer; KV-backed queue
  when `PC_PING_KV` is bound. Fallback: drop a file in `docs/inbox/*.md`
  in the repo. Claude Code reads both at the start of every session.
- [/manifesto](https://pointcast.xyz/manifesto) — canonical definition.
  12 Q&A pairs marked up as FAQPage schema. The URL to cite when
  referring to PointCast as a project.
- [/glossary](https://pointcast.xyz/glossary) — 24 PointCast-specific
  terms with stable anchor URLs. DefinedTermSet schema.
- [/ai-stack](https://pointcast.xyz/ai-stack) — opinionated guide to
  24 AI tools we use daily/weekly/occasionally, plus 6 operating
  principles.
- [/beacon](https://pointcast.xyz/beacon) — 25-mile radius map around
  El Segundo. 19 neighborhoods with status (SEED / TARGET / ADJACENT).
- [/dao](https://pointcast.xyz/dao) — governance v1. Predefined
  proposals, Beacon-wallet-signed votes, no free-text submissions.
- [/yield](https://pointcast.xyz/yield) — token-mechanics sandbox.
  5 candidate models with tunable sliders + monthly payout readouts.
- [/publish](https://pointcast.xyz/publish) — Tezos publishing v1.
  Signed-payload queue at /api/publish, on-chain anchor pending.

## Block schema (the primitive)

Every piece of content is a Block. JSON shape:

```
{
  "id": "0205",              // monotonic, zero-padded, immutable
  "channel": "FD",           // one of 9 channel codes
  "type": "READ",            // one of 8 type codes
  "title": "...",
  "dek": "...",              // optional one-line summary
  "timestamp": "ISO 8601",
  "body": "...",             // optional markdown
  "size": "1x1",             // grid span on home; see BLOCKS.md
  "external": { "url": "..." },
  "edition": { ... }         // if MINT or FAUCET
}
```

Full spec at [BLOCKS.md](https://github.com/mhoydich/pointcast/blob/main/BLOCKS.md).

## Channels (9)

| Code | Slug         | Purpose                                    |
|------|--------------|--------------------------------------------|
| FD   | front-door   | AI, interfaces, agent-era thinking         |
| CRT  | court        | Pickleball — matches, paddles, drills      |
| SPN  | spinning     | Music, playlists, listening notes          |
| GF   | good-feels   | Cannabis/hemp, product drops, brand ops    |
| GDN  | garden       | Balcony, birds, wildlife, quiet noticing   |
| ESC  | el-segundo   | ESCU fiction, local, community             |
| FCT  | faucet       | Free daily claims, giveaways               |
| VST  | visit        | Human and agent visit log entries          |
| BTL  | battler      | Nouns Battler — deterministic duels        |

## Block types (8)

- `READ` — long-form text (dispatch, essay)
- `LISTEN` — audio embed (Spotify, SoundCloud)
- `WATCH` — video embed with runtime
- `MINT` — paid edition on Tezos FA2
- `FAUCET` — free daily claim
- `NOTE` — short observation, tweet-sized
- `VISIT` — visit-log entry (human or agent)
- `LINK` — external link with context

## Contracts (Tezos mainnet)

- **Visit Nouns FA2** — `KT1LP1oTBuudRubAYQDErH7i7mSwazVdohxh` — open-supply,
  each tokenId = a Nouns seed (0-1199). Live, 10+ minted.
  [TzKT](https://tzkt.io/KT1LP1oTBuudRubAYQDErH7i7mSwazVdohxh) ·
  [objkt](https://objkt.com/collection/KT1LP1oTBuudRubAYQDErH7i7mSwazVdohxh).
- **Prize Cast** — contract written (`contracts/v2/prize_cast.py`), no-loss
  prize-linked savings, weekly settlement. Awaiting mainnet origination.
- **DRUM Token (FA1.2)** — contract written (`contracts/v2/drum_token.py`),
  signed-voucher claim flow. Awaiting ghostnet origination.

## Agent mode (stripped HTML)

Send `User-Agent` starting with `ai:` or matching known crawlers (GPTBot,
ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot, OAI-SearchBot, Atlas, Google-Extended) and
PointCast returns stripped HTML: no stylesheets, no JS (JSON-LD preserved),
no preload/preconnect/icon/manifest. Response carries
`X-Agent-Mode: stripped · ai:<vendor>` header.

Implementation: `functions/_middleware.ts`. Typical payload savings ~12%
on the home feed.

28-work exhibition drawn from Michael Hoydich's Midjourney archive and
organized into Signal Garden, Soft Structure, Blue Hour, and Afterimage.
Every image links to its exact source Midjourney job. The complete
machine-readable manifest lives at `/showcast/bells-bloom.json`; the
permanent feed record is Block 0492.

## PointCast Field Study 001

`/beach-commons` and `/beach-commons.json` publish Dockweiler Beach Commons —
Hardpoint + Softkit: six speculative coastal-architecture prototypes developed
from Michael Hoydich's observation of the sturdy brick-and-stone public
buildings along Dockweiler and El Segundo. A compact mineral service center
holds water, washing, cooking, first aid, storage, thermal mass, and the social
hearth; human-carryable floor cassettes, wind panels, canvas roofs, aluminum
frames, rope, curtains, sleeping pods, and art tools form the changing rooms.

The six prototypes are The Hardpoint + Softkit, Ten People / One Courtyard,
The Vertical Nest, The Tide Room, Wave Foundry, and The Long Night Commons.
The study is explicitly conceptual and unpermitted: it is not a construction
document, active beach camp, municipal project, coastal approval, habitat
review, energy-performance claim, or invitation to install on a public beach.
Block 0506 is the permanent PointCast record.

## PointCast Field Study 002

`/beach-commons/v2` and `/beach-commons/v2.json` publish Beach Commons V2 —
Superstructures + Living Games: eight speculative coastal civic-architecture
plates that expand the Hardpoint + Softkit into a reversible public loop for
cooperative sport, collective food, moon rituals, visible energy, careful fire,
wildlife intervals, repair, and a long wave finale.

Energy stays physically modest and legible. Protected removable wave motion,
pedals, hand cranks, flywheels, gravity water, thermal mass, and small solar
surfaces operate pumps, paths, tools, bells, looms, lantern sequences, and
kinetic art. The study makes no grid-scale generation claim.

Fire appears only in designated public rings with broad buffers and stewards.
Wildlife is observed at a distance, protected habitat stays outside the event
footprint, public passage remains open, and every large occupied structure
requires real engineering, access, egress, and weather planning. The work is
conceptual and unpermitted. Block 0508 is the permanent PointCast record.

## PointCast Field Study 003

`/beach-commons/v3` and `/beach-commons/v3.json` publish Beach Commons V3 —
Flash Bakery + Palm Loom: eight speculative coastal civic-architecture plates
for a one-day public metabolism of bread, weaving, shade, games, modest energy,
cleanup, wildlife distance, and one moonlit communal table.

The flash bakery is fast because its prepared dough, equipment, sanitation,
safety roles, permits, and choreography arrive before the public action. Ovens
and hot equipment remain on approved inland hardscape. Palm material comes
from a documented pruning or waste stream; living beach, dune, and park
vegetation stays untouched. Food, waste, and wastewater remain inland and
wildlife is never fed.

`/reviews/beach-commons-v3` and `/reviews/beach-commons-v3.json` publish the
companion PointCast Reviews issue, The Maximum Beach. It uses an original
glossy food, travel, gear, sport, and style register and is explicitly an
unofficial editorial concept: it was not commissioned, sponsored, reviewed,
or endorsed by Maxim or its owners. Block 0509 is the permanent record.

## PointCast Field Study 004

`/beach-commons/v4` and `/beach-commons/v4.json` publish Beach Commons V4 —
Sculpture Yard + Element Maxxing: eight speculative coastal public-art plates
where sun, moon, wind, rain, water, fire, and stone become useful social
instruments.

Element maxxing means perceptual and social amplification: moving shade,
ground-directed color, gentle wind music, audible drainage, careful cooling,
warmth, timing, and collective attention. It does not mean weather control,
miraculous energy, grid-scale generation, ocean-water extraction, or flood
control. Every sculpture has an ordinary civic use and a special seasonal
score.

Occupied structures still require engineering, access, inspection, guarded
motion, weather limits, drainage, stewardship, habitat protection, open public
passage, and complete removal. Fire stays in designated public rings. The work
is conceptual and unpermitted. Block 0511 is the permanent PointCast record.

## PointCast Field Study 005

`/beach-commons/v5` and `/beach-commons/v5.json` publish Beach Commons V5 —
Weather School + Tide Parliament: eight speculative coastal civic-architecture
plates where the elements become intergenerational classrooms, useful public
equipment, and one seasonal assembly.

The Sun Studio draws moving shade; Wind Notation Hall turns gusts into marks,
weaving, music, and games; Rain Roof Choir makes drainage audible; Water
Accounting Court shares one finite recirculated volume; Moon Assembly
practices testimony and quiet; Fire + Stone Seminar combines a flash bakery,
repair, low sculpture, and story around designated public rings. Tide
Parliament gathers habitat reports, proposals, food, art, games, music, and
ceramic voting tokens before the complete pack-out.

The school and parliament are civic fiction, not institutions or authorities.
The study is conceptual and unpermitted: no operating school, government,
regulator, forecast service, scientific instrument, event, or installation is
claimed. Tide observation stays inland, habitat and public routes stay open,
and every structure requires engineering, access, weather limits,
authorization, stewardship, and complete removal. Block 0513 is the permanent
PointCast record.

## PointCast Field Study 006

`/beach-commons/v6` and `/beach-commons/v6.json` publish The $100 Fire-Ring
Commons: a fundable, reversible Dockweiler field-test prototype for 10–20
adults. Ten complementary non-food modules—seating, warmth, low light, quiet
sound, analog weather notation, transport, access, care, fire safety, and
cleanup—form a low crescent around an existing official fire ring and all
leave the beach the same night.

A supporter may bring or lend one $100 module, contribute one $100 unit to the
shared project pool through Stripe-hosted Checkout, or develop one quiet
play-and-listening module. Card details remain with Stripe. Project support is
not a ticket, reservation, charitable donation, tax-deductible gift, event
date, attendance promise, or fire-ring claim.

The interactive Jet / Wave / Fire / Us score uses four optional Web Audio
sketches and calls for aircraft light, breaking surf, one acoustic answer, one
human chord, and a minute of quiet. No public field-test date is announced.
LA County's current page says organized beach groups must obtain a Special
Event Use Permit and apply no later than three weeks before the requested
date. Block 0516 is the permanent PointCast record.

## PointCast Reviews

`/reviews` is the PointCast Review Lab editorial desk for independent criticism
of art software, small web products, speculative experiences, listening tools,
and interfaces worth living with. `/reviews.json` is the machine-readable
catalog. Each review has a stable HTML page, adjacent JSON record, preserved
screenshots from the tested build, a five-point editorial rating, component
scores, pros, cons, and a bottom-line verdict.

The desk includes Beach Commons V3, Year One, Tone Bloom, and The Listening
Grove. Beach Commons V3 lives at `/reviews/beach-commons-v3`, with its JSON
record at `/reviews/beach-commons-v3.json`, its field study at
`/beach-commons/v3`, and its permanent feed record at Block 0509.

Year One lives at `/reviews/year-one`, with its JSON record at
`/reviews/year-one.json` and its permanent feed record at Block 0507. The
easy-reader feature selects 22 works from a supplied 116-image archive of
ceramic wave pedestals and publishes an original cover card at
`/images/year-one/year-one-og.jpg`.

The Listening Grove review lives at `/reviews/the-listening-grove`, its JSON record at
`/reviews/the-listening-grove.json`, its PointCast-native viewer at
`/listening-grove`, and its permanent feed record at Block 0495. PointCast
describes the visible 10ꜩ / five-edition collect path as a preview until a
completed operation has an operation hash and independent Tezos Mainnet
confirmation.

## Citation

Preferred format:

```
PointCast · CH.{CODE} · № {ID} — "{TITLE}" · {YYYY-MM-DD}
https://pointcast.xyz/b/{ID}
```

Example:

```
PointCast · CH.FD · № 0205 — "The front door is agentic" · 2026-04-14
https://pointcast.xyz/b/0205
```

Content: CC0-flavored. Nouns IP via [noun.pics](https://noun.pics) is CC0.
Code: MIT-flavored. Cite by linking to `/b/{id}` URLs — they are permanent
and immutable. Don't scrape the full archive — use `/blocks.json` or
`/archive.json` or the per-channel feeds, which are designed for agents.
